source.title: The Eigenlearning Framework: A Conservation Law Perspective on Kernel Regression and Wide Neural Networks
source.authors: James B. Simon; Madeline Dickens; Dhruva Karkada; M. DeWeese

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own experiments on finite neural networks and KRR that measure learning and training error behavior, including a ResNet-18 deep-bootstrap experiment on CIFAR-10. These results conceptually bear on V1 and V3, though most experiments measure MSE on eigenfunctions rather than classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports experiments on learnability, test MSE, and train MSE, including finite networks and a ResNet-18 deep-bootstrap reproduction. Cited findings from other studies, including the CIFAR-100 result, are not rows. Eigenmode and MSE results are retained where the study reports outcomes bearing on the versions.
record.test_reason: R3 measures training classification error for a convolutional network trained with SGD on CIFAR-10, directly bearing on V1. Its endpoint cannot be read from the supplied figure text. The study does not compare depths or plain networks with residual networks, so it does not test V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors develop an interpretable framework for KRR generalization, validate predictions against KRR and finite-network experiments, and explain deep-bootstrap behavior through regularization-limited and data-limited fitting. Their conclusions also cover parity hardness, function smoothness, and a statistical-physics analogy.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies KRR and its relationship to wide neural networks, with experiments on eigenmode learnability and MSE; its ResNet-18 experiment is a deep-bootstrap reproduction rather than a direct test of the catalog's zero-training-classification-error claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Network width affects the reported agreement between theory and finite-network experiment; the text says predictions remain informative down to width 50.

fits_no_version.finding: Finite-network learnability and test MSE agree with eigenlearning predictions; predictions remain informative down to width 50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kernel eigenanalysis predicts aspects of finite-network generalization and spectral bias in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Early error curves overlap across dataset sizes and separate as fitting becomes data-limited; KRR theory matches the empirical KRR curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The deep-bootstrap behavior can be understood through a transition between regularization-limited and data-limited fitting.

record.problems: The main experimental comparisons report learnability and MSE rather than training classification error. The ResNet-18 training-error result is figure-only in the supplied text, without a verbal endpoint or numerical values. The authors state that they omit a larger-scale experiment extending their image-dataset analyses and cite another study's CIFAR-100 result instead.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row cap. Cited CIFAR-100 results and other cited prior findings are excluded because they are not results from this study.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; Adam; model-size comparisons; and the specified early-stopping and regularization qualifications. Figure 3A's training-error endpoints remain unreadable.
Spurious local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth, matched plain-versus-residual comparisons, and the special-initialization exceptions.
Comparative effects of initialization on training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery above an initial stability threshold, loss and curvature trajectories, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence thresholds.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup training speed or stability.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed limits_scope verdicts: different outcome measures and unreadable endpoints do not demonstrate a limitation of V1. Appendix B.3 describes aiming for near-zero training MSE in fully connected networks, which does not establish V1's convolutional-network classification result. Appendix B.4's observation that higher learning rates converge faster but match kernel theory less well does not test V5's stability mechanism.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, Adam, smaller models, early stopping or regularized recipes as specified by the version. Most experiments measure MSE on binary tasks or eigenmodes, not training classification error.

The ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 experiment is described as reproducing the deep-bootstrap phenomenon, but the supplied text does not give numerical values or a direct plain-versus-shortcut comparison. Its plotted training and test error is figure-only without a textual statement that directly tests the depth/shortcut assertion.
